knowledge_gaps: Reproducibility needs explicit example counts, prefix selection, deletion counts, shuffle seeds, diagnostic frequency, and GPU-time limits. The loader provides no user IDs, so user-level bootstrap and category aggregation require a documented mapping or sampling directly from routed user_train histories.

Deleting and compacting histories changes both evidence and positional inputs. Preserving the last item during shuffling does not isolate these effects. Length-one histories and ineffective shuffles need explicit eligibility rules.

The existing scorer handles per-position item scores; scoring 100 candidates from one final feature requires a specified tensor-shape adapter. Optimistic strict-above tie ranking can also disagree with the predictor's actual top-10 ordering.

The selected probe measures temporal sensitivity, but does not operationalize repeated interests or specific relevance. Its connection to future validation gains remains untested; future-potential 8 is optimistic and implementation-difficulty 3 understates integration work.

The mandatory full-catalog recommendations for twenty training users need a separate execution path. Diagnostic sampled candidates cannot replace that requirement. Repeated diagnostic-guided selection can also overfit the fixed validation users.
